<SUMMARY>
The week of May 22-29, 2026, was marked by intensifying geopolitical competition, particularly in advanced technology and critical minerals. Huawei announced a significant semiconductor breakthrough, while US entities, including Microsoft and Nvidia, unveiled new AI hardware and reaffirmed supply chain strengths amidst growing demand. Export controls targeting China intensified, though their effectiveness was questioned by the US Commerce Department. In critical minerals, Japan initiated deep-sea rare earth exploration, the US secured a Greenland rare earth deal, and China tightened its grip through mining controls and leverage with Greenland. The Middle East conflict continued to drive global economic uncertainty, influencing commodity markets and raising concerns about inflation and job losses in Japan and Europe.
</SUMMARY>

<EWS>
The stability achieved at the Trump-Xi Summit is projected to be temporary, with geopolitics expected to revert to competition. Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that AI advancements could destabilize societies globally. There is a grave risk that Russia could pose to northern Europe if it gains control of the Arctic’s Bear Gap. The U.S. Commerce Department admitted failure to enforce AI export controls on China, highlighting a significant enforcement gap. Beijing is set to prolong rare-earth curbs and engage in economic retaliation against Tokyo. The Iran war is rattling energy markets, prompting the OECD to slash global growth forecasts and predicting potential recessions globally if the conflict extends into 2027, with the EU facing a potential loss of 1.3 million jobs. Taiwan Semiconductor's CoWoS capacity is experiencing strain, intensifying the AI chip packaging battle and posing a vulnerability in the AI compute supply chain.
</EWS>

<EXEC>
**Asia:**
Huawei Technologies announced on May 25 that it will produce industry-leading semiconductors using a new technology in five years. SK Group and Foxconn are engaged in talks that could signal deeper Taiwan-Korea AI supply chain ties. AMD committed more than $10 billion to Taiwan's AI supply chain. The U.S. expanded semiconductor export bans to Chinese overseas entities. The Commerce Department admitted failure to enforce AI export controls on China. Huawei hit a process wall, while TSMC's SoIC deepens AI chipmaker lock-in for AI chipmakers. A Chinese university built a 3D chip design tool tailored to Huawei LogicFolding architecture. China's "safe and reliable" procurement list first added domestic AI chips to accelerate the replacement of US products like Nvidia's. China forbade top AI experts from leaving the country without approval. Nvidia pledged $150 billion a year in Taiwan, with its Constellation Campus breaking ground. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) is described as being at the absolute center of the AI compute supply chain. SK Hynix plans to double wafer capacity due to an AI memory shortage. SurplusGLOBAL secured Korean Patents for AI-Powered Export Control Automation Technology.

**Europe:**
The European Union’s €20 billion ($23.3 billion) investment plan for five massive artificial intelligence data centers is encountering delays and funding issues. STMicroelectronics shares rose over 15% as the company strengthens its AI infrastructure position and sees recovering demand in automotive and industrial markets. Wolfspeed Inc. shares rose over 13% following its strategic expansion into AI data center power solutions. A British chipmaker is aiming to take on the world. Foxconn, Radiall, and Thales inaugurated Tessalia to produce over 50 million "made in Europe" components annually. Europe unveiled a sweeping tech sovereignty plan to boost chips and AI.

**Americas:**
Microsoft Corp. announced the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a new desktop form factor supercomputer for agentic development, developed with Nvidia Corp.’s RTX Spark processor. Bitcoin miner Hive is racing to build what it calls Canada's largest private AI data center. Jensen Huang stated Nvidia has enough CPU and GPU supply for "very, very robust growth," despite constrained supply and pressure from Vera Rubin and RTX Spark. Marvell entered the AI network fray with 102.4 Tbps switch silicon. TSMC taps Nvidia accelerated computing to drive next-gen semiconductor fabs. TSMC weighs AI pricing power against overseas fab margin pressures. The AI chip packaging battle intensified, with Taiwan Semiconductor's CoWoS capacity facing strain, prompting Intel's EMIB-T to step in and support Google's TPU supply chain. Intel stock is up 250% in 2026. Polar Semiconductor and Nexperia partnered on US-based power MOSFET manufacturing for EVs.
</EXEC>

<REE>
**Americas:**
The Trump Administration accelerated US-China critical minerals decoupling, with the Pentagon’s 2027 defense deadline reshaping a $30 billion magnet market. USA Rare Earth selected Cherokee County, South Carolina, for a new rare earth metal and magnet manufacturing operation. USA Rare Earth expanded its commitment to France with plans for additional investment in the French Rare Earth Ecosystem. The U.S. secured a Greenland rare earth deal in a bid to cut China reliance. Defense-driven demand powered a surge in US listings by mining firms.

**Asia:**
Japan will develop a deep-sea drone to search for rare earth mineral resources in the seabed near a remote island. China kept rare earth pressure on Washington after the Trump Summit. Beijing is set to prolong rare-earth curbs and economic retaliation against Tokyo. China tightened its grip as Greenland blocked a critical rare earth project. China imposed mining controls on strategic minerals starting June 15.

**Africa:**
The EU is betting billions on South Africa as China tightens its grip on critical minerals. Africa faces new competition for critical minerals investment as the U.S. secured a Greenland rare earth deal. The EU's investment in South Africa’s critical minerals sector was explained. The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) imposed Cobalt Export Quotas to stabilize prices and attract investment. DRC’s Congo Lithium Royalty Tax Hike increased to a 10% strategic rate in 2026.
</REE>

<GEO>
**Asia:**
The Trump-Xi Summit produced stability, but the arc of geopolitics will bend back toward competition. The Sino-Serbian relationship is becoming a blueprint for strategic autonomy. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced on June 2nd that the Japanese government will significantly strengthen supplies of paint thinner and other chemical products by allowing raw materials to be supplied directly from petroleum refiners. Japan is incrementally rebalancing its foreign policy beyond China and the US, seeking further hedges despite its alliance with the US and economic relationship with China. Latest U.S.-China Agriculture Talks expanded purchasing pledges beyond soybeans.

**Europe:**
The European Union’s €20 billion ($23.3 billion) investment plan for five massive artificial intelligence data centers is floundering, with delays and funding issues. Russia could pose a grave risk and must not be allowed to control the Arctic’s Bear Gap.

**Americas:**
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that "the United States right now is a global leader on AI," but "that lead is not irreversible." Activists were arrested protesting Secretary Rubio’s new attacks on lifesaving global AIDS and health programs during Senate Foreign Relations Committee Testimony.

**Oceania:**
The Atlantic Council Commission on AI laid a roadmap for US leadership in the age of AI. The US is struggling with its adversaries over the future of AI.
</GEO>

<MILITARY>
**Asia:**
China says it drove away a Dutch warship near the disputed Paracel Islands.

**Europe:**
The Norwegian defense minister warned Russia could pose a grave risk and must not be allowed to control the Arctic’s Bear Gap, potentially allowing it to hit northern Europe.

**Americas:**
Westmag, an American manufacturer of drone motors and robot actuators, emerged from stealth today with $11 million in seed funding. USA Rare Earth Chief Global Policy Officer Gregory Bowman was appointed to the Department of War Science, Technology and Innovation Board.
</MILITARY>

<CONCLUSION>
The week saw a continued global scramble for technological and mineral dominance, primarily driven by US-China competition in AI and semiconductors. China's domestic advances and restrictive export/exit policies indicate a deepening strategic autonomy, countered by US efforts to secure supply chains and expand export controls. Europe's ambitions in AI infrastructure faced funding hurdles, while Japan and the EU engaged in critical mineral diplomacy and exploration. Military concerns centered on Russian expansion in the Arctic and maritime tensions in Asia. The economic ripple effects of the West Asia conflict emerged as a significant global destabilizer.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
India’s data center sector is experiencing rapid growth, leading to substantial land acquisitions across new markets. Major investments are creating new infrastructure corridors, driven by hyperscale cloud operators and AI providers. PepsiCo introduced its premium energy drink, Adrenaline Rush, to the Indian market, targeting Gen-Z. Oyo’s IPO plans are back on track after securing Sebi approval. IT stocks led a recovery in Indian markets, reversing losses despite geopolitical tensions and foreign selling pressures. The ongoing crisis in West Asia has struck a harsh chord for Indian small enterprises (MSMEs), leaving them vulnerable to significant setbacks with anticipated decreases in production and revenue due to mounting trade obstacles. Tech rivalry between the US and China and wars in the Middle East are reshaping India’s foreign policy choices. India’s Semiconductor Ecosystem is maturing, and ASML is taking notice. Anthropic's AI rollout in India occurred. News indicated China stopped India's vehicle, and powerful friends gave treasure, which reduced New Delhi's increased concern. The concept of Atmanirbhar (self-reliant) versus Nirbhar Bharat (dependent India) was discussed. Indian companies achieved better-than-expected profits in the March quarter, supported by tax cuts and easy money, but the ongoing Iran conflict creates an energy shock expected to impact future company earnings.
</INDIA>

<WEST_ASIA>
Food price increases in Japan are accelerating, with the number of products subject to higher prices potentially reaching 20,000 items this year, linked to tensions in the Middle East spreading through supply chains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surpassed 51,000, driven by AI advancements and strong corporate earnings, despite geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties impacting investor sentiment, including the Middle East. US stocks declined before the bell on Tuesday as traders parsed the latest developments in the Middle East. Wall Street was set to open lower even as AI and data center companies soared, due to Mideast news. Commodity markets have spent the past three months performing an extraordinary balancing act despite one of the most significant disruptions to global energy flows in decades. Following an updated situational assessment and a ceasefire declaration, the Home Front Command eased safety guidelines for northern areas of Israel. The IDF announced it killed a Hamas Nukhba terrorist who participated in the abduction of hostage Hersh Goldberg-Polin during the Oct. 7 attack. Hezbollah and IDF traded fire despite a nominal truce, as Lebanon-Israel talks are set to resume in the US. US Secretary of State Rubio told lawmakers that Iran’s supreme leader appears more active as talks continue, and Tehran has agreed to discuss previously off-limits aspects of its nuclear file. President Donald Trump blasted "fake news reports" that negotiations with Iran had stalled, asserting that they have been "going on continuously." President Trump has been facing intense backlash from MAGA loyalists after shifting his stance on Iran’s army. The OECD slashed its global growth forecast due to the Iran war rattling energy markets. The EU could lose 1.3 million jobs due to an energy price surge linked to the Iran war, according to the Commission. The OECD predicts a spate of recessions globally if the Iran conflict drags into 2027. Economists state the Iran War will impact energy costs in the US. UAE lenders are leading the way in Middle East AI adoption. The UAE expanded its AI push with a new leadership development program. Israel's energy decade is reshaping global power, posing a challenge for Israel. US sanctions were placed on an Iran crypto exchange.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
Looking forward, the global technology landscape will continue to be shaped by intense strategic competition between major powers, particularly concerning AI and advanced semiconductor manufacturing, where national policies will increasingly drive supply chain diversification and resilience efforts. Critical minerals will remain a flashpoint, with nations actively seeking to secure domestic and allied sources while navigating existing dependencies and emerging trade restrictions. The persistent instability in West Asia is likely to further exacerbate global energy market volatility and contribute to broader economic headwinds, necessitating robust risk management and adaptive foreign policy responses.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
